about: Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC) is a UK quantum computing company spun out of the University of Oxford in 2017, now based in Reading, building superconducting quantum computers using its patented dimon coaxmon technology and offering access through cloud platforms and on-premises systems. Customers are enterprises, governments and research bodies; it has data centre deployments with Digital Realty in New York and Tokyo. Funding includes a 100 million dollar Series B in 2023 and a total above 400 million. B2B deep-tech with little public brand awareness.

wiki.title: Oxford Quantum Circuits
wiki.text: Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC) is a British company that develops superconducting quantum computers. It was founded in 2017 by the physicist Peter Leek as a spin-out from the Department of Physics at the University of Oxford. It is based in Reading.

about: Bright Machines is a San Francisco company offering microfactories that use software-defined robotics and AI for flexible electronics and high-tech manufacturing, selling to customers like Nvidia, Microsoft and other electronics makers. Founded in 2018, it has raised about 437 million dollars, with investors including Nvidia and Microsoft. Revenue comes from hardware, software and services. B2B industrial technology with low consumer awareness.

nLIGHT is a US manufacturer of semiconductor and fibre lasers for industrial cutting and welding, microelectronics, defence and directed-energy applications. Customers include machine-tool makers and defence primes such as the US Department of Defense. Founded in 1991 and based in Camas, Washington, it listed on Nasdaq (LASR) in 2018. Revenue is roughly 200 million dollars. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Wrench Group is a Marietta, Georgia, home services company providing residential heating, cooling, plumbing, electrical and appliance repair and replacement through a network of local brands across the US, formed by combining many regional service businesses. It is private equity owned and one of the largest home service providers in the country, with funding shown at about 1.3 billion dollars. Customers are homeowners. Local service brands have regional recognition; the Wrench name itself is little known.
cb_desc: Wrench Group offers home repair, replacement and...

about: Polar Semiconductor is a US semiconductor foundry in Bloomington, Minnesota that manufactures power, sensor and automotive-grade chips on 200mm wafers for customers in automotive, industrial and aerospace markets. It earns money through contract wafer manufacturing. It was formerly owned by Sanken Electric and Allegro MicroSystems and was recapitalised in 2024 with a large US CHIPS Act award and private investment, with the Crunchbase total funding at about $298 million. B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Polar Semiconductor manufactures automotive-..

about: Allegion is an Irish-domiciled security products company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ALLE), spun out of Ingersoll Rand in 2013. It makes locks, door hardware and access control under brands including Schlage, Von Duprin, LCN and CISA, selling to building owners, contractors and homeowners in North America and Europe, with revenue of about $3.7 billion. Schlage is a familiar US hardware brand, while the parent is a B2B name.

wiki.title: Allegion
wiki.text: Allegion plc is an American Irish-domiciled provider of security products for homes and businesses.

about: Western Digital is a San Jose, California storage company, listed on Nasdaq (WDC), which makes hard disk drives and, until the 2025 spin-off of Sandisk, flash storage. Its brands include WD, WD_Black and SanDisk. Customers are cloud providers, PC makers and consumers, with revenue of about $10 billion. Strong consumer brand in data storage, and it has run motorsport sponsorships.

wiki.title: Western Digital
wiki.text: Western Digital Corporation, doing business as WD, is an American data storage company headquartered in San Jose, California. Established in 1970, the company is one of the world's largest manufacturers of hard disk drives (HDDs).

about: Landis+Gyr is a Swiss maker of smart electricity, gas and water meters and grid management systems, headquartered in Cham, Switzerland and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (LAND). Customers are utilities worldwide, with strong positions in North America and Europe, and revenue is about $1.7 billion. Previously owned by Toshiba and the Innovation Network Corporation of Japan. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Landis+Gyr
wiki.text: Landis+Gyr Group AG, formerly known as Bayard Group, is a publicly listed, multinational corporation operating in over 30 countries and headquartered in Cham, Switzerland. Landis+Gyr makes meters and related software for electricity, gas and water utilities.

about: AirTrunk is an Australian hyperscale data center operator, founded in 2014 by Robin Khuda and based in Sydney, with campuses across Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia and Indonesia, serving cloud and AI customers such as Microsoft, Google and Alibaba. It was acquired in 2024 by Blackstone and CPP Investments for about A$24bn. Revenue is earned from long-term data center capacity contracts. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: AirTrunk
wiki.text: AirTrunk is an Australian data centre company founded by Robin Khuda in 2015, and sold to Blackstone for A$24 billion. The company operates more than 3 GW of operating and planned capacity across 20 sites in six countries: Australia, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, Hong Kong, and India.

about: Switch is a Las Vegas data center and technology infrastructure company, with large campuses in Nevada, Georgia, Michigan and Texas and Europe and Asia, known for its SUPERNAP facilities and Tahoe Reno park. Customers include cloud, tech and enterprise firms. It was taken private in 2022 by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors for about $11bn. Private. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness, though it has been involved in Las Vegas sports and naming deals.

wiki.title: Switch
wiki.what: Electrical component that can break an electrical circuit
wiki.text: In electrical engineering, a switch is an electrical component that can disconnect or connect the conducting path in an electrical circuit, interrupting the electric current or diverting it from one conductor to another. The most common type of switch is an electromechanical device consisting of one or more sets of movable electrical contacts connected to external circuits. When a pair of contacts is touching, current can pass between them, while the contacts are separated no current can flow.

wiki.title: Switch (company)
wiki.text: Switch, Inc. is an American company based in Las Vegas, Nevada, that develops and operates the SUPERNAP data center facilities and provides colocation, telecommunications, cloud services, and content ecosystems.

about: EdgeConneX is a Herndon, Virginia data center developer and operator that builds edge and hyperscale facilities in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific for cloud providers, content companies and enterprises. It has been owned by EQT Infrastructure since 2018, which took over from Providence Equity. Private, with funding mainly debt. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Edgecore Digital Infrastructure is described by Crunchbase as an experienced global data center company based in Denver, Colorado, with industries listed under information technology. Funding shown is about $3.1bn with the latest round in October 2026. No further detail on campuses, customers or owners is given in the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Edgecore Digital Infrastructure is an experienced global dat..

about: VEON is a Dubai-headquartered digital operator and telecom holding company, listed on Nasdaq (VEON), with mobile, digital financial services and entertainment businesses in Ukraine (Kyivstar), Pakistan (Jazz), Bangladesh (Banglalink) and Kazakhstan (Beeline Kazakhstan) after selling its Russian assets. It serves over 150 million customers. Revenue is about $4bn. Jazz and Kyivstar are strong consumer brands in their countries, with local sponsorship activity.

wiki.title: Veon (company)
wiki.text: VEON Ltd., also known as VEON Group, is a multinational telecommunications and digital services company. Headquartered in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, the company is publicly traded on the U.S.-based Nasdaq stock exchange.

about: Vertiv is a Westerville, Ohio maker of critical digital infrastructure, supplying power, cooling, racks, thermal management and services to data centers, communications networks and industrial sites. Customers include hyperscalers, colocation providers and enterprises, with revenue near $9-10bn. It was formerly Emerson Network Power and listed on the NYSE (VRT) in 2020 via a SPAC with GS Acquisition Holdings. B2B brand, known in the data center industry, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Vertiv
wiki.text: Vertiv Holdings Co. is an American provider of infrastructure and services for data centers, communication networks, and commercial and industrial environments. Headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, Vertiv has around 34,000 employees worldwide, operating in more than 40 countries and with 30 manufacturing and assembly facilities.

about: Wolfspeed is a Durham, North Carolina maker of silicon carbide materials and power devices, used in electric vehicles, renewable energy, fast charging and industrial power, with wafer fabs in North Carolina and New York. It went through a Chapter 11 restructuring in 2025 and emerged with debt largely converted to equity. Customers include automakers and power electronics firms. Listed on the NYSE (WOLF). B2B semiconductor supplier with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Wolfspeed
wiki.text: Wolfspeed, Inc. is an American developer and manufacturer of wide-bandgap semiconductors, focused on silicon carbide materials and devices for power applications such as transportation, power supplies, power inverters, and wireless systems. The company was formerly named Cree, Inc.

about: Khazna Data Centers is an Abu Dhabi-based operator of wholesale data centers, serving hyperscalers, cloud providers, enterprises and government clients in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey and Italy. It is the largest data center operator in the UAE, a subsidiary of Emirati tech group e& and the AI firm G42, and has multi-gigawatt AI-focused expansion plans. Earns capacity leasing revenue. B2B infrastructure with little consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Khazna Data Centers operates state-of-the-art wholesale dat...

about: Serverfarm is a data center company based in El Segundo, California, offering a portfolio of data center infrastructure including colocation, wholesale and build-to-suit facilities, with sites in North America, Europe and Asia. It serves enterprise, cloud and technology customers and earns long-term capacity lease revenue. It has raised very large capital, reported at about $5.3 billion. Backed by institutional investors. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Serverfarm is a data center company providing a complet...

about: STACK Infrastructure is a Denver-based provider of wholesale data center capacity and campuses for hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises, operating in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific. Founded in 2013 and backed by infrastructure investors including IPI Partners, it has raised more than $9 billion across equity and debt. Revenue comes from long-term capacity leases. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: STACK Infrastructure provides digital infrastructure solutions...

about: AtlasEdge is a UK-based edge data center platform, founded in 2021 as a joint venture between Liberty Global and DigitalBridge, offering colocation and interconnection near end users across Europe in around 30 markets. Customers are cloud, content, telecom and enterprise users. It reported about 2.2 billion funding. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

VSE Corporation is an Alexandria, Virginia-based aviation and distribution services company (Nasdaq: VSEC), supplying parts distribution, repair and maintenance for aircraft and components via its Aviation segment (Precision Aviation Group acquisition in 2024) and a fleet segment serving US military and commercial fleets. Revenue is about $1 billion. Customers include the US government, airlines and operators of fleets. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

CyrusOne is a US data centre operator headquartered in Dallas, Texas, owning and leasing large colocation and hyperscale facilities across the US, Europe and Asia for cloud providers, enterprises and AI workloads. Taken private in 2022 by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners for about 15 billion dollars. Founded 2000 as a Cincinnati Bell unit. Revenue comes from long-term leases. B2B infrastructure business, known in technology circles.

wiki.title: CyrusOne
wiki.text: CyrusOne, Inc. owns and operates over 40 carrier-neutral data centers in North America, Europe, and Asia, where it provides colocation and peering services. It is headquartered in Dallas, Texas and is owned by funds managed by Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners.

about: CACI International is a US information technology and expertise services provider to government, delivering intelligence, cyber, communications, enterprise IT and mission support for the US Department of Defense and intelligence agencies, with revenue of about $8 billion and some 25,000 employees. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, founded in 1962. Listed on NYSE (CACI). B2B government contractor with little consumer visibility.

wiki.title: CACI
wiki.text: CACI International Inc. is an American multinational aerospace and defense company headquartered in Northern Virginia. CACI provides services to many branches of the US federal government including defense, homeland security, and intelligence.

about: CONMED is a US medical technology company making surgical devices for orthopedics, general surgery, gastroenterology and robotics, including arthroscopy products, electrosurgery, endoscopy systems and its AirSeal insufflation system. Customers are hospitals and surgery centres in over 100 countries, with revenue of about $1.3 billion. Headquartered in Largo, Florida. Listed on NYSE (CNMD). B2B medical brand with limited consumer awareness.

Atlanta-based digital infrastructure company, DC BLOX, building data centres and subsea cable landing stations in the southern US. Funding shown is about $2.5 billion. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness. Customers are cloud, content and enterprise firms that need connectivity in smaller US markets. Founded 2011 and backed by infrastructure investors. B2B only, with no consumer awareness. The company serves cloud, content and enterprise customers in markets such as Georgia, Florida and the Carolinas.

Brazilian data centre and telecom company based in Vinhedo, Sao Paulo, a subsidiary of Digital Realty. Customers are cloud providers and enterprises. B2B infrastructure brand with no consumer awareness. Customers include Microsoft, Google and Oracle, which lease capacity from its 10+ sites in Brazil and the region. B2B only, with no consumer awareness. Ascenty has about 30 data centre sites across Brazil and Chile, and its owner Digital Realty operates globally.

Xpansiv is a New York-based market infrastructure and data company that runs the CBL exchange for environmental commodities, including carbon credits, renewable energy certificates and other sustainability instruments, with data and registry services for traders and corporates. Customers are energy companies, corporates and financial institutions buying and retiring offsets. Backed by institutional investors, with funding of about 718 million dollars shown. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Swedish data centre operator based in Falun, running large low-carbon colocation sites powered by renewable electricity and used by cloud and technology companies. Privately owned and growing. B2B infrastructure provider with no consumer brand awareness.

El Paso, Texas company described in the input as providing connectivity and digital solutions, with cloud management and private network tags. No customers, scale or ownership are stated. It may be a small telecom or network services provider serving businesses in the region. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: KUBRA is a Tempe, Arizona customer experience management and billing technology company serving utilities, telecoms and governments with bill presentment, payments, outage maps and communications. It is privately held and private-equity backed. Crunchbase shows about $500 million in funding. B2B software and services, low consumer awareness.
cb_desc: KUBRA provides customer experience management...

about: Lutech is a Milan-based Italian IT services and system integration company, offering cloud, cybersecurity, data and digital transformation services to enterprises and public bodies, backed by Apax Partners. It grew through acquisitions, including Sinergy and others, and has thousands of employees. Crunchbase shows about 400 million in funding. B2B, little consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Lutech is an engineering company that designs..

about: Endava is a London-headquartered technology services company that provides software development outsourcing, digital engineering, AI and consulting to large clients, mainly in financial services, payments, insurance, healthcare and telecom, with delivery centres across Europe, Latin America and Asia. Founded in 2000, it is listed on the NYSE under DAVA, with revenue of around $1.1 billion. B2B IT services brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Endava
wiki.text: Endava plc is a British technology services company headquartered in London, providing outsourced software development and IT consulting services. Its American depositary shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol DAVA.

about: Meter is a San Francisco company that offers networking as a service, designing and installing managed wired and wireless networks, switches, firewalls and software for businesses, charged by subscription. Founded in 2015, it has raised about $255 million. Customers are offices, schools, warehouses and retailers. B2B infrastructure with growing recognition among IT teams and little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Metre
wiki.text: The metre is the base unit of length in the International System of Units (SI). Since 2019, the metre has been defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of ⁠1/299792458⁠ of a second, where the second is defined by a hyperfine transition frequency of caesium.

wiki.title: Meter (company)
wiki.what: American network as a service company
wiki.text: Meter is an American technology company that provides internet infrastructure for businesses. Headquartered in San Francisco, it was founded by Sunil and Anil Varanasi in 2015 to build secure enterprise-grade networks.

about: Skylo is a Mountain View, California company that provides non-terrestrial network connectivity, letting ordinary smartphones, IoT devices and vehicles send messages and emergency alerts via geostationary satellites. It works with mobile carriers and device makers, and is the satellite provider behind the Google Pixel satellite SOS and Samsung Galaxy features, plus Verizon and Deutsche Telekom partnerships. It earns service fees from carriers and manufacturers and has raised over $200 million. Its technology reaches consumers, but the Skylo brand is mostly known to the telecoms industry.

wiki.title: Skylo
wiki.text: Skylo is a satellite communications company headquartered in Mountain View, California that provides connectivity based on 3GPP Rel-17 for SMS, sensor data, and other low-bandwidth services, with plans that include voice calls and limited data for consumer devices. It connects regular cellular devices to satellites through existing satellite networks so they can work when terrestrial cellular coverage is not available, using a system that works with satellite operators, mobile networks, and device makers.

about: Cape is an Arlington, Virginia mobile carrier and security company, founded in 2021, that builds a privacy-focused cellular network which limits location and identity tracking for users. It targets government, defense, intelligence and high-risk professionals as customers, plus privacy-minded consumers, and has raised about $196 million, including backing from Andreessen Horowitz. B2B and government-focused brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Cape
wiki.what: Sleeveless outer garment of varying lengths, sometimes attached to a coat
wiki.text: A cape is a clothing accessory or a sleeveless outer garment of any length that hangs loosely and connects either at the neck or shoulders. They usually cover the back, shoulders, and arms. They come in a variety of styles and have been used throughout history for many different reasons.

about: CoreSite is a Denver-based operator of data centres and interconnection hubs in major US metros such as Los Angeles, Silicon Valley, New York, Chicago and Northern Virginia. It was a listed REIT before being acquired by American Tower for about $10 billion in 2021. Customers are enterprises, cloud providers and networks. B2B brand with little consumer recognition.

Conclusion is a Dutch IT services group, based in Utrecht, made up of dozens of specialised IT companies delivering software, cloud, data, security and consulting services to Dutch and Belgian enterprises and government. It employs several thousand people and has been backed by private equity (Bencis and, later, others). B2B IT firm with limited public brand awareness.

about: MariaDB is an open-source relational database company, with a US base in Milpitas, California, and origins in Finland, created by the original MySQL founders. It sells MariaDB Enterprise Server, SkySQL cloud database service and related tools to businesses and cloud customers. It went public on the NYSE through a SPAC in 2022 (MRDB), and was taken private by K1 Investment Management in 2024. B2B software brand, known to developers, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: MariaDB
wiki.text: MariaDB is a open-source relational database management system (RDBMS) sharing a common heritage with MySQL, from which it was forked in 2009 by original MySQL developers following Oracle Corporation's acquisition of Sun Microsystems, with the intent to keep it free and open-source software under the GNU General Public License.

about: Hexatronic Group is a Swedish fibre optic infrastructure company based in Gothenburg. It makes and sells fibre cables, ducts, connectivity and installation systems for telecom operators, data centres and utilities, with operations in Sweden, Germany, the US, the UK and Asia, and acquisitions such as Raycap's fibre business. Revenue is in the billions of Swedish kronor. Customers are network builders and telecoms. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under HTRO, and the Crunchbase figure shows SEK 1.1 billion raised, latest in May 2026. B2B supplier with little public brand awareness.

Zetrix is a Malaysian blockchain and digital infrastructure company based in Petaling Jaya, Selangor, that builds the Zetrix public blockchain, digital identity and tokenisation solutions for government and enterprises. It is linked to MYEG Services, the e-government services provider, and has been publicised for the Zetrix AI chain and Zetrix wallet in Malaysia and Asia. Crunchbase shows about $40 million raised, latest February 2026, and flags the company as listed. Mostly B2B and government projects, moderate awareness in Malaysia.

wiki.title: List of Tetris variants
wiki.text: This is a list of variants of the game Tetris. It also includes officially licensed Tetris sequels, as well as unofficial clones. In 2017 Guinness World Records reported Tetris to be the game with most official versions released, at 220, over 65 different platforms.

about: Eclairion is a French data computing centre in Bruyeres-le-Chatel, in the Essonne area south of Paris, offering high-performance computing and AI infrastructure hosting for public research bodies, industry and technology clients. It earns from hosting, capacity and service contracts. Crunchbase shows about 160 million in funding, with the latest round in February 2025, suggesting investment in capacity expansion. Privately held. B2B infrastructure with little brand awareness outside the HPC and data centre sector.
cb_desc: Eclairion is a data computing center that provides high..

about: Axway is an API management and managed file transfer software company, with its French roots and a US base in Scottsdale, Arizona. Its platform helps enterprises, banks and governments integrate systems, exchange data securely and publish APIs, and it has thousands of customers worldwide. It is listed on Euronext Paris (AXW) and was formerly a unit of Sopra, with Sopra Steria still a major shareholder. Revenue is near EUR 300M. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Axway Software
wiki.text: Axway Software is a French-American publicly held information technology company that provides software tools for enterprise software, enterprise application integration, business activity monitoring, business analytics, mobile application development and web API management.

about: Systex Corporation is a Taiwan-headquartered information technology services company (the data places it in Hong Kong), providing software, system integration, cloud, financial information systems and cybersecurity solutions to banks, securities firms, governments and enterprises across Taiwan, China and Southeast Asia. It is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (6214). Funding of about NT$3.97B appears in the data for 2024. B2B IT brand known among enterprise buyers, with low consumer awareness.

Upsun is a Paris-based cloud platform, from the company formerly known as Platform.sh, which gives developers and businesses a tool to build, deploy and manage web applications across multiple environments, with automated preview environments and cloud hosting. It earns subscription and usage fees from agencies and software firms. Crunchbase shows about 175 million dollars raised from venture investors. A B2B developer tools brand with no consumer profile.
cb_desc: Upsun provides tools to build, deploy, and manage web...

about: Pivot3 was a hyperconverged infrastructure company that supplied integrated storage and computing systems, especially for video surveillance, to enterprises and governments. It was based in Austin, Texas, with Colorado listed in the input, and its assets were acquired by Quantum Corporation in 2021. It was a B2B technology brand known to IT and security integrators, with no consumer visibility. It is no longer an independent company.

Xtera was a McKinney, Texas network equipment and services company that sold subsea and terrestrial optical transmission systems, including Raman-amplified long-haul and unrepeatered undersea networks, to telecom operators and energy companies. It filed for bankruptcy and was acquired by Infinera in 2017. It was a B2B telecom brand with no consumer profile and is now defunct. Its customers were carriers and operators of subsea cables.

India's largest staffing and business services company, based in Bangalore and founded by Ajit Isaac, with operations in general staffing, IT staffing, facility management, security services and logistics. Customers are thousands of enterprises across sectors, and it places or manages several hundred thousand workers. Brands within the group include Quess IT Staffing, Conneqt, Allsec and Terrier Security Services. It is listed on the NSE and BSE, and Fairfax-linked Thomas Cook India originally founded and controlled it. Largely B2B with limited consumer recognition, though the name is known in Indian HR circles.

LendInvest is a UK property finance company that provides buy-to-let mortgages and short-term bridging and development loans, using a digital platform and funded by institutional and retail investors. Headquartered in London; founded 2008. Funding shown is around 4.1 billion dollars, likely including debt lines. Originated billions of pounds of loans. Privately held, with a small bond listing. Known to landlords and property investors, with a limited consumer profile.
cb_desc: Lendlnvest is a property fintech company that offers buy-to-le..

about: TMX Group is a Toronto-based Canadian financial exchange operator running the Toronto Stock Exchange, TSX Venture Exchange, Montreal Exchange and clearing houses, plus data and analytics (TMX Datalinx) and Trayport trading software. It earns listing fees, trading fees, and data subscription revenue, with revenue of roughly C$1.5bn. Listed on the TSX (X). B2B financial infrastructure, with high name recognition in Canadian finance but little consumer visibility.

wiki.title: TMX Group
wiki.text: TMX Group Limited is a Canadian financial services company that operates equities, fixed income, derivatives, and energy markets exchanges. The company provides services encompassing listings, trading, clearing, settling and depository facilities, information services as well as technology services for the international financial community.

about: Brookfield is a Toronto and New York-based global alternative asset manager (Brookfield Corporation and Brookfield Asset Management, NYSE/TSX: BN, BAM), managing over $1 trillion in assets in infrastructure, renewable power, real estate, private equity and credit. Founded in 1899. Investors are pensions, sovereigns and individuals. Corporate brand known in finance; it owns brands via real estate (Brookfield Place) and investments such as Westinghouse.

Victory Capital is a US asset management firm headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, listed on Nasdaq (VCTR), that owns multiple independent investment franchises and manages around 300 billion dollars in mutual funds, ETFs and separate accounts. It sells through financial advisers and institutions and has grown by acquiring firms such as USAA Asset Management and Amundi US. Founded as a KeyCorp unit and independent since 2013. B2B financial brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Victory Capital
wiki.text: Victory Capital Holdings, Inc. is an American financial services company headquartered in San Antonio, Texas that focuses on investment management. Outside the US, it also has investment professionals in London, Hong Kong and Singapore.

about: SEGRO is a UK real estate investment trust that owns, manages and develops modern warehouses and light industrial property, including urban warehousing and large distribution centres, in the UK and continental Europe. Customers are logistics, retail and e-commerce tenants, with revenue from rent. Headquartered in London, with a portfolio valued around 20 billion pounds. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (SGRO). B2B property company, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Segro
wiki.text: SEGRO plc is a British property investment and development company based in London, England. It develops and invests in property located in the United Kingdom and Continental Europe focusing on areas around cities and key transport hubs. The firm switched to Real Estate Investment Trust status when REITs were introduced in the United Kingdom in January 2007. The company is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index.

about: Western Union is a global money transfer company, enabling consumers to send money across more than 200 countries and territories through agents, retail locations, online and its app, plus business payments. Revenue is about $4 billion from transfer fees and foreign exchange. Headquartered in Denver, Colorado, and founded in 1851 as a telegraph company. Listed on NYSE (WU). In 2025 it agreed to acquire Intermex. Very recognisable global consumer brand, particularly among migrant communities.

wiki.title: Western Union
wiki.text: The Western Union Company is an American multinational financial services corporation headquartered in Denver, Colorado.

about: CBRE Investment Management is a global real assets investment manager, part of CBRE Group, investing in real estate, infrastructure and renewable energy on behalf of pension funds, insurers and sovereign wealth funds, with more than 150 billion dollars of assets under management. Its Toronto office appears in Crunchbase, though the firm is run from Radnor, Pennsylvania. Revenue comes from management fees. The parent CBRE Group is listed on NYSE (CBRE). B2B asset manager with little consumer awareness.

CI Financial is a Toronto-based wealth and asset management company offering mutual funds, advisory and wealth services in Canada, the US and Australia through CI Global Asset Management, Corient and others, with hundreds of billions of dollars under management and administration. Customers are retail investors and advisors, with revenue from management fees. Taken private in 2025 by a Mubadala Capital-led investor group, previously listed on the TSX (CIX). Known among Canadian investors.

wiki.title: CI Financial
wiki.text: CI Financial is a Canadian investment management company based in Toronto, Ontario. It offers investment management and wealth management services targeted to high net worth retail investors, as well as brokerage and trading services to portfolio managers and institutional investors.

about: Cloud Capital is a global investment management firm based in Washington, DC, according to Crunchbase, which classifies it under angel investment and finance. Crunchbase shows about $1.85 billion in funding as listed, which may be assets raised. Its investment focus, ownership and portfolio are not described in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Cloud Capitalisa globalt i investment management firm...

about: Propel is a UK-based asset finance firm in Newport, Wales, according to the input. Details are limited. The input says it provides a range of asset finance products and has about $2.1 billion of funding. Based in Wales. Propel appears to operate as a non-bank lender, and funding of about $2.1 billion is shown. Other products and customers are not described. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Propel specializes in providing a wide range of asset finance...

wiki.title: Propel (company)
wiki.text: Propel, Inc. is an American fintech software company that builds services for low income families. It is best known for Providers, a mobile app that allows users to track their Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) balances and other government benefits. Approximately one quarter of American households receiving SNAP benefits are enrolled in the app.

about: Columbus, Ohio, asset manager founded in 2022 by Vivek Ramaswamy and Anson Frericks, offering ETFs and an anti-ESG shareholder engagement approach. In 2025 it merged with Asset Entities and adopted a bitcoin treasury strategy, becoming a listed company (Nasdaq: ASST). Funding shown is about $2.4 billion. Brand is known mainly in investing and political circles. Strive manages ETFs and also runs the Strive bitcoin treasury company, and Vivek Ramaswamy has stepped back from the executive chair.

San Francisco- and Fort Worth-based alternative asset manager, founded 1992 by David Bonderman and Jim Coulter, managing about $250 billion across private equity, growth, real estate, impact and credit. Customers are pension funds and institutions; revenue from fees and carry. Listed on Nasdaq (TPG). B2B finance brand with moderate visibility in sports ownership and investment. It employs about 1,000 people and has offices in 20 cities, and it also owns stakes in sports teams and entertainment ventures.

Investcorp is a global alternative asset manager founded in 1982 and headquartered in Manama, Bahrain, with offices in New York, London, Riyadh and Abu Dhabi, managing tens of billions of dollars in private equity, real estate, credit and infrastructure. Clients are institutions and wealthy investors, mainly in the Gulf and internationally. Its shares are listed on the Bahrain Bourse. Known in Gulf finance circles, and with some sports and event sponsorship, but little general consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Investcorp
wiki.text: Investcorp is a global alternative investment company headquartered in Manama, Bahrain. Founded in 1982, the firm invests across private equity, real assets, credit, infrastructure, insurance asset management, and other alternative investment strategies. As of July 2026, Investcorp reported $62.3B worth of assets under management.

about: Willis Lease Finance is a Coconut Creek, Florida aircraft engine leasing company, listed on Nasdaq (WLFC), which owns and leases jet engines and aircraft parts to airlines and runs asset management and engine trading services. Its portfolio is valued at several billion dollars. Customers are commercial airlines and maintenance firms worldwide. B2B with limited visibility beyond aviation finance.

Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners is a London-based investment manager, founded in 2007, that invests in renewable energy, power grid, storage and data centre infrastructure, with projects in the US, UK and Australia, such as the Supernova data centre power campus. It manages funds for institutional investors, with several billion dollars of capital. B2B with low public brand awareness.

Aukera is a Brussels based investment company active in asset management and energy, according to Crunchbase. It invests in energy-related assets and projects, with funding of about $760 million recorded. The input gives no detail on its specific holdings, clients or ownership. It appears to be a financial investor serving institutional or private capital rather than consumers, so brand visibility is likely very low. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Aukera is an investment company that specializes i.

about: Focus Financial Partners is a St. Louis based partnership of wealth management firms, providing fiduciary advice to high-net-worth families through registered investment advisers across the United States and abroad. It acquired many independent advisory firms and collected fees on client assets under management. It was listed on Nasdaq (FOCS) and was taken private in 2023 by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice and Stone Point Capital in a deal valued around 7 billion dollars. It is B2B and low in public brand awareness.

wiki.title: Focus Financial Partners
wiki.text: Focus Financial Partners Inc. is an American company that invests in independent, fiduciary wealth management firms, being listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol FOCS. Headquartered in New York City, it was incorporated in 2004 by Ruediger (Rudy) Adolf, Rajini Kodialam and Leonard (Lenny) Chang.

about: Stem is a US clean energy technology company that sells AI-driven energy storage software (Athena) and battery systems for commercial buildings, utilities and solar projects. Customers are businesses and project developers. Founded in 2009, it went public on the NYSE in 2021 (STEM). Crunchbase lists Houston, Texas, after a headquarters move from the Bay Area. B2B with limited public brand awareness.

Altruist is a US digital custodian and portfolio management platform for independent financial advisors, with a low-cost brokerage, trading and reporting tools, plus Hazel, its AI tax planning tool. Founded in 2018 and based in Culver City, California, it has raised venture capital from firms such as Insight Partners, Vy and GIC. Customers are RIAs and their clients. B2B fintech with limited public brand awareness.

wiki.title: Altruism
wiki.what: Concern for the well-being of others
wiki.text: Altruism is concern for the well-being and life of others independently of personal benefit or reciprocity.

about: Miami International Holdings (MIAX) is a US financial exchange group, based in Princeton, New Jersey, with options exchanges (MIAX Options, Pearl, Emerald), futures and equities venues, and the Bermuda Stock Exchange. Customers are trading firms and brokers, paid via transaction fees. Listed on the NYSE (MIAX) after a 2025 IPO. B2B with a limited public profile.

wiki.title: Miami International Holdings
wiki.what: American exchange and clearing house company
wiki.text: Miami International Holdings, Inc. (MIH), trading as MIAX, is an American company formed in 2007 that operates global financial exchanges and execution services.

about: Virtus Investment Partners is a US multi-boutique asset manager, based in Hartford, Connecticut, with a series of specialist investment affiliates and about $170 billion of assets under management, serving individuals, institutions and advisors. Listed on the NYSE (VRTS). B2B financial brand with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Virtus Investment Partners
wiki.text: Virtus Investment Partners, Inc. is an American company which operates as a multi-manager asset management business, comprising a number of individual affiliated managers, each having its own investment process and brand, and the services of unaffiliated sub advisers.

about: DigitalBridge is a Boca Raton, Florida investment firm that owns and manages digital infrastructure assets, including data centres, cell towers, fibre networks and small cells, through managed funds (Vantage Data Centers, Switch, DataBank, Landmark). It was formerly Colony Capital and is listed on the NYSE (DBRG), with about 100 billion dollars of assets under management. In 2025 SoftBank agreed to acquire it. Customers are institutional investors. Well known in infrastructure investing, but low consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: DigitalBridge
wiki.what: American private equity real estate firm
wiki.text: DigitalBridge Group, Inc. is a global digital infrastructure investment firm. The company owns, invests in and operates businesses such as cell towers, data centers, fiber, small cells, and edge infrastructure. Headquartered in Boca Raton, DigitalBridge has offices in Los Angeles, New York, Denver, London, and Singapore. As of June 2025, DigitalBridge had US$106 billion of assets under management.

about: Slate Asset Management is a Toronto alternative asset manager focused on real estate and infrastructure, managing funds such as Slate Grocery REIT and Slate Office REIT, with around 7 billion dollars of assets. Customers are institutional and retail investors. A financial vehicle with limited consumer brand awareness.

Apex Group is a Bermuda-headquartered global fund administration and financial services provider, offering fund administration, depositary, ESG, middle-office, banking and digital solutions to asset managers, private equity and institutional clients. It has offices in dozens of countries, employs over 12,000 people and administers more than $3 trillion in assets. Privately owned and sponsor-backed (Genstar and others), reaching a valuation of several billion dollars. B2B with little consumer awareness.

Finnfund is the Finnish development finance company, based in Helsinki, owned by the Finnish state and other institutions. It invests in companies and projects in developing countries, particularly in Africa, Asia and Latin America, in areas such as renewable energy, financial services, agriculture and forestry. Founded in 1980. It is a development financier with no consumer product brand, so it is a weak F1 sponsorship fit.

Acadian Asset Management is a Boston-based quantitative investment adviser, founded in 1986, which runs global and regional equity and multi-asset strategies for institutions, using systematic models. The company was formerly BrightSphere Investment Group and rebranded as Acadian Asset Management in 2025, listed on the NYSE (AAMI). It manages over $100 billion for pension funds and others. It is a B2B brand with no consumer recognition.

wiki.title: Acadian Asset Management
wiki.what: Asset management firm based in Boston
wiki.text: Acadian Asset Management is an American investment management company headquartered in Boston with additional offices in London, Singapore and Sydney. The company is noted for its usage of Quantitative analysis and strategies when making investment decisions.

about: Connor, Clark & Lunn Infrastructure is a Toronto-based investment manager that invests in middle-market infrastructure and energy assets, such as power generation, renewables and utilities, in North America and Europe. It is part of Connor, Clark & Lunn Financial Group, a Canadian employee-owned asset manager with hundreds of billions in assets. It serves institutional investors, so has no consumer brand.
cb_desc: Connor, Clark & Lunn Infrastructure invests in midd..

about: Patria Investments is a Cayman Islands-registered alternative asset manager focused on Latin America, with operations in Sao Paulo, offering private equity, infrastructure, real estate, credit and public equities funds to institutional and wealthy investors. It manages more than 40 billion dollars and was formed in 1994, with Blackstone and later Itau as investors. It is listed on Nasdaq (PAX) since 2021. Financial brand known to investors, with no consumer profile.

Belgian financial market infrastructure group based in Brussels that settles securities transactions and holds securities in custody for banks, brokers and institutional investors worldwide. Operates the Euroclear Bank international central securities depository and national depositories in France, Belgium, the Netherlands and the Nordics. Earns fees from settlement, custody and collateral services, with tens of trillions of euros in assets under custody. Owned by Euroclear Holding, whose shares are held by market users. In the news for holding immobilised Russian central bank assets. Pure B2B with low public awareness.

wiki.title: Euroclear
wiki.text: Euroclear, or the Euroclear Group, is a Belgium-based financial market infrastructure group that specialises in the central securities depository (CSD) segment. It traces its origins to the Euro-clear System developed in 1968 by Morgan Guaranty in Brussels to settle trades on the then developing eurobond market. The service was rebranded Euroclear in 1990.

about: Inseego is a San Diego company making wireless products for the 5G and 4G market, such as mobile hotspots, MiFi devices, fixed wireless access routers and indoor and outdoor 5G equipment, plus cloud management services for businesses and carriers. Customers are mobile operators such as Verizon and T-Mobile, enterprises, and consumers via carrier channels. Revenue is from hardware sales and subscriptions. Listed on Nasdaq (INSG). Brand recognition mainly with carriers and business buyers, and moderate among mobile hotspot users.

StepStone Group is a global private markets investment firm, based in New York, that provides customised investment programmes, funds and advisory services across private equity, infrastructure, private debt and real estate for pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and wealthy individuals. It manages or advises on around 700 billion dollars or more in assets under management and advisement. Founded in 2007, it is listed on Nasdaq (STEP). Institutional finance brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: StepStone Group
wiki.text: StepStone Group LP is a global private markets firm providing customized investment, portfolio monitoring and advice to investors. StepStone covers primary fund investments, secondary fund investments and co-investments across private equity, real estate, infrastructure and real assets, and private debt.

about: Betashares is an Australian fund manager and the country's largest independent issuer of exchange traded funds, based in Sydney, with products such as the A200 and NDQ index ETFs, plus thematic and income funds and a direct investing platform. Customers are retail investors, advisers and institutions, and revenue comes from management fees. Founded in 2009, it manages more than 40 billion Australian dollars. Crunchbase shows about 300 million Australian dollars of funding. Well-known investor brand in Australia with a growing public profile.

The RMR Group is a Newton, Massachusetts-based alternative asset manager that manages commercial real estate and related businesses, including REITs and operating companies such as Diversified Healthcare Trust, Office Properties Income Trust, Seven Hills Realty Trust, Service Properties Trust and Industrial Logistics Properties Trust. Listed on Nasdaq (RMR). Revenue is management fees, based on the assets of the companies it manages. Crunchbase shows about 100 million dollars of funding in 2025. Institutional brand, not consumer-facing.

wiki.title: Beltone
wiki.text: Beltone is a hearing aid company founded in 1940 and headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. Its products are sold in the United States, Canada, and more than 40 other countries. The Beltone Hearing Care Foundation, a 501(c)(3) charitable organization, was established in 2014 to donate hearing instruments to those in need. In North America, Beltone has over 1,500 independently owned centers that provide hearing screenings, fittings, follow-up care, and aftercare services.

about: Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) is a New York-based infrastructure investment manager that owned and ran assets in energy, transport, water and waste, with holdings such as Gatwick Airport, Edinburgh Airport and Biffa. It was acquired by BlackRock in 2024 for about 12.5 billion dollars and has been integrated into BlackRock. Investors are pension funds and sovereign wealth funds. B2B asset manager with little consumer awareness, though its portfolio companies are visible.

wiki.title: Global Infrastructure Partners
wiki.text: Global Infrastructure Partners, LLC (GIP) is an American infrastructure investment fund making equity and selected debt investments across markets worldwide. GIP's main headquarters are located in New York City, U.S. and its equity investments are based on infrastructure assets in the energy, transport and water & waste sectors. GIP employs approximately 150 investment and operational professionals and has offices in New York, London, Stamford, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Mumbai, Delhi, Singapore and Hong Kong. In total as of 2023, its portfolio companies employ approximately 100,000 people, according to the company website. BlackRock acquir

about: Pico is a New York-based technology services provider for the global financial markets, offering low-latency network infrastructure, market data feeds, managed hosting and the Corvil analytics platform to banks, exchanges and trading firms. Investor backed, with funding of about 372 million dollars recorded. Revenue comes from recurring service contracts with financial institutions. Operates data centre connections in major trading hubs. B2B specialist with little consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Pico is a provider of technology services for the global financi.

about: Cohen and Steers is a New York-based asset manager specialising in real assets and alternative income, including listed real estate securities, infrastructure, commodities and preferred securities. Founded in 1986, it manages roughly $80 billion to $90 billion for institutional and retail investors through mutual funds, ETFs and separate accounts. It is listed on the NYSE (CNS). Revenue comes from management fees. Well known among financial professionals, with little public brand awareness.

Hong Kong-based digital financial services company, Oriente, building consumer lending and financial infrastructure for emerging markets, with operations in Asia and Latin America. Venture and credit-backed, offering digital loans through partners and its own apps. Customers are underbanked consumers and small businesses. Brand mostly known to fintech investors, with only regional consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Oriente is building anew digital financial services infrastructu...

about: Fidelity Investments, the privately owned financial services group based in Boston and controlled by the Johnson family, which runs mutual funds, retirement plans, brokerage, wealth management and workplace benefits for tens of millions of customers, with trillions of dollars in assets. Founded in 1946, it employs tens of thousands of people. Fidelity International is a separate company outside the US. Very high consumer brand awareness in the US, with a history of sponsorships in sport and the arts.

wiki.title: Fidelity
wiki.what: Quality of faithfulness or loyalty to another person or group
wiki.text: Fidelity is the quality of faithfulness or loyalty. Its original meaning regarded duty in a broader sense than the related concept of fealty. Both derive from the Latin word fidēlis, meaning "faithful or loyal". In the City of London financial markets it has traditionally been used in the sense encompassed in the motto "my word is my bond".

about: Calgary-based investment management firm that runs mutual funds and portfolios for Canadian investors, with products across equity, income and balanced strategies and a retail distribution through financial advisors. Revenue is from management fees on assets that run into billions of Canadian dollars. Founded in the 1990s. Moderate recognition among Canadian financial advisors, and low awareness among the general public. It is part of the wider Canadian asset management industry, where funds are sold through advisors, banks and online platforms.
cb_desc: Canoe Financial is an investment management firm...

about: French IT services and financing group that designs, finances and manages digital transformation for companies, through technology leasing, device-as-a-service, IT infrastructure and digital services, operating in about 15 countries with thousands of staff. Customers are large corporations, public bodies and small businesses, and revenue is several billions of euros. Listed on Euronext Paris (ECONB) and based in Puteaux. B2B business with strong profile among IT buyers, and a small consumer presence.

wiki.title: Econocom
wiki.text: Econocom Group SE is a European business-to-business (B2B) digital services provider specialized in digital transformation for private and public organizations. Founded in 1974 by Jean-Louis Bouchard under the name Europe Computer Systèmes (ECS), the group operates across the digital value chain, including workplace solutions, IT and audiovisual infrastructure, and technology asset financing.

about: Chicago-based investment research and data firm founded in 1984 by Joe Mansueto, best known for mutual fund ratings (the star ratings), Morningstar Direct, PitchBook private-markets data, Sustainalytics ESG and DBRS Morningstar credit ratings. Customers are financial advisers, asset managers, retail investors and institutions, paying subscriptions and licensing and asset-based fees via its wealth arm. It has about 11,000 employees, revenue around 2 billion dollars and trades on Nasdaq (MORN). Widely recognised in finance, less so among general consumers.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 1999: check it is still independent and operating

about: South Korea's dominant search engine and internet platform, offering Naver search, webtoons, shopping, maps, payments (Naver Pay), cloud and AI (HyperCLOVA X) as well as the LINE messaging stake via LY Corp. Earns from advertising, commerce and fintech, with annual revenue about 10 trillion won. Headquartered in Seongnam, Gyeonggi; founded 1999. Listed on the Korea Exchange (035420). Very strong consumer brand in Korea and Japan with Webtoon global reach, and active in cultural and esports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Naver
wiki.text: Naver is a South Korean online platform operated by the Naver Corporation. The company's products include a search engine, email hosting, blogs, maps, and mobile payment.
